solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seeing the future of a vicar only upset them initially

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word them

explanation.surface: A clergyman's knack of prophecy unsettles his parishioners from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A VICAR ONLY into CLAIRVOYAN; 'initially' adds T from 'them'. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with second sight is said to see what is coming, so the adjective describes foresight.

clue.text: US state exercise set up ancient weapons

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: sport is physical exercise

explanation.surface: Some American state has staged a demonstration of old-time armaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SPORT into TROPS beneath CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: These were spiked iron devices strewn on the ground to maim horses in old warfare.

clue.text: Sprays also designed to protect painful back

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so one piece goes round the other
designed means arranged to a plan, so the letters are reordered
back means read in reverse

parts.note: painful means sore

explanation.surface: Medicated sprays are also made to shield an aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' gives AOLS; 'back' reads as the anatomical back but is the reversal signal, and 'to protect' wraps the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pressurised cans that spray out a fine mist, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Figure house doctor should support Republican

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting below, so the house-and-doctor pair goes under R

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A political wish that the family GP should back the Republican candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure; the shorter form is a recognised variant.

clue.text: Reserved and rode off looking embarrassed

indicators.note: off here means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an embarrassed face looks red

explanation.surface: A shy rider set off on horseback, blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reserved, such as a table, has been booked or requested in advance.

clue.text: Tested when on top of state education

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of means placed above the other pieces

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Pupils are examined once they reach the peak of the state school system.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to analyse or test a metal or substance, so the past forms correspond.

clue.text: Tasty — to an unspecified number eating hot stew

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: some means an indefinite quantity

indicators.note: stew means to be in a muddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spicy stew pleases any number of diners who tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' gives OTH, which 'eating' sets between the two other pieces; 'stew' looks like the dish being eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe food that is delicious and appetising; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cold shoulder — of lamb?

definitions.meaning: to give someone the cold shoulder is to snub or ignore them
a shoulder of lamb is a joint the butcher sells

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold shoulder' reads as a dish of leftover meat; in fact it is a verb meaning to snub, and the dash leads to the butcher's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to ignore them deliberately; a butcher's joint of meat is also called this.

clue.text: Cougars will accept he does

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: cougars are big cats

explanation.surface: Older women on the prowl will take a chance on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is the verb 'to do' meaning swindles, not the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, so the third-person verbs match.

clue.text: Easily irritated, one leaves the City in turmoil

indicators.note: in turmoil means in disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: With markets in chaos, a jumpy trader walks out of London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leaves' removes I from THE CITY; 'in turmoil' rearranges the rest. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tetchy is irritable and quick to take offence, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Slow student has a right turn

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A slow learner driver manages a right turn.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this tempo marking means slow and broad.

clue.text: Bent receiver must have one way

parts.note: a satellite dish receives signals
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A crooked fence must have a single route out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' suggests a handler of stolen goods, but here it is a satellite dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for crooked or corrupt.

clue.text: Scrape by, accepting blunder could be a show of contempt

parts.note: to rasp is to scrape roughly

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone barely scraping through, making a mistake, gets mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing this rude noise with the tongue and lips signals derision.

clue.text: Minor problem with answer for one opening

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces the other

parts.note: a hitch is a small snag
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A small snag arises over the reply to a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch is an opening, such as one in a ship's deck or a wall.

clue.text: Kept control of parasites in whales

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a pod is a group of whales
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Marine biologists monitored the parasite numbers within a whale group.
explanation.definitionFit: Policing an area means keeping order there, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Pass poor dosser getting such blisters

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rough sleeper on a mountain pass is getting lip sores from the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges DOSSER into DSORES. A dosser is British slang for a rough sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Herpes causes small painful sores around the lips, the blisters the clue refers to.

clue.text: Low returns on diamonds must mean inevitable ruin

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across entry

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: returns means is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, like cattle

explanation.surface: A fall in yields on gemstones spells financial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MOO into OOM; 'Low returns' reads as poor profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a dreadful fate that cannot be escaped.

clue.text: British Rail originally invested in new toilet book

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside
new signals the letters made into a fresh order
originally picks the opening letters of British and Rail

explanation.surface: Old railway funds were sunk into refurbishing station lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives LIETTO, and 'invested in' sets the initials inside it; British Rail was the old UK national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera is called its book or this word.

clue.text: Advance making progress on the backs of others

definitions.meaning: to advance by jumping ahead, skipping stages

definitions.text: making progress on the backs of others
definitions.meaning: describes the children's game where players vault over crouching companions

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: in the playground game you move forward by leaping over others' backs.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump over rivals or stages is to advance; the game itself involves vaulting over bent backs.

clue.text: A final cut short, unfortunately

indicators.note: cut short means the closing letter is removed

parts.note: last means final

explanation.surface: A cup final ended early, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses regret or sorrow, much like sadly.

clue.text: Student son's arrest reported

indicators.note: reported means as heard spoken

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son; collar is slang for arrest, as police nabbing a suspect

explanation.surface: News reports describe a student's son being detained.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner or someone engaged in study is a pupil or student.

clue.text: Viceroy, king and ambassador in front of disreputable club

indicators.note: in front of means placed before the following piece

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub

explanation.surface: A royal delegation of king and envoy is seen outside a sleazy nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of the Ottoman Turkish governor of Egypt, a vice-regal post.

clue.text: Family doctor at home is number one in team

parts.note: kin means relatives
GP is a general practitioner
in means at home

explanation.surface: The family doctor relaxing at home is the team's top player.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important person in a group, on whom the rest depend, is called this.

clue.text: Discourage study covering a politician

indicators.note: covering means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a den is a private study
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A report about an MP discourages further study.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen enthusiasm is to discourage it or make it less lively.

clue.text: Drop it off, being sluggish

indicators.note: off means amiss, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling someone to stop fussing because they are lethargic.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpid creature is inactive and lethargic, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A cat's tiny bits

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom's is a cat's

explanation.surface: A kitten's toys torn to small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the smallest particles of matter, so the phrase describes them loosely.

clue.text: Polish group rejected seductive scheme

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or refine

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a party is a group

explanation.surface: A Polish political faction was turned down after a seduction plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb. 'rejected' turns PARTY into YTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plot using sexual enticement to compromise a target, as in espionage.

clue.text: Plant seen in your cocoa, intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sprout seems to have turned up in a cup of cocoa.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a spiky-leaved evergreen from the Americas, an example of a plant.

clue.text: FT magazine article found in office?

parts.note: the Financial Times is a newspaper
a clip or clipping is an article cut out of a publication

explanation.surface: The setter plugs their own newspaper and a magazine feature found on an office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: This small bent-wire fastener is standard stationery in any workplace; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Supply food for a disheartened type in credit

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
disheartened means the middle letters are removed

explanation.surface: Providing meals for a gloomy sort of person on account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the heart, YP, of the word, and 'in' puts the result with A inside the credit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterers provide meals for events, so the verb means providing provisions.

clue.text: Show agreement, backing academic type

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A professor signals support for a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A downward movement of the head signals assent or approval.

clue.text: Offer false hope to new girl's agent on lacking energy

indicators.note: new signals the letters made into a fresh order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A talent agent tires of stringing a new young client along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes E from GIRLS AGENT ON; 'new' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive someone with empty promises is to keep them waiting hopefully, an idiom.
